title: Annotatio IV §.XXIV: Torun n.10–13 — not naked signs; deny only local/corporal mode; IPSA SUBSTANTIA body and blood
pass_a_gloss: As to Presence, they would sincerely believe and say with Irenaeus that the Sacred Supper consists of two things, namely earthly and heavenly. As to exhibition, they would pronounce even in the Wittenberg Professor’s own VII words without all pretence: Ours (the Reformed) name the Sacramental Signs Exhibitive not by reason of promises, use and fruit alone, but by reason of the heavenly matter, as they love to speak — or because in them, through external and visible elements, heavenly and invisible things are not only signified or somehow represented but also dispensed. Which very thing not only single Doctors (e.g. Trelcatius in words I alleged in the German Tract) but also the public Reformed Confessions — specially the Torun, which is also our Marchic — most clearly enunciate. For so the said Confession on the Supper holds from n. 10 through n. 13 inclusive: Yet we by no means establish naked, empty, void Signs, but rather ones truly exhibiting at once what they signify and seal, as most certain media and efficacious instruments through which Christ’s Body and Blood — and so Christ Himself with all His benefits — is exhibited or offered to each who eats, but to believers conferred, given, and accepted by them as salutary and life-giving food of the soul. We also by no means deny the true presence of the Body in the Supper, but only the LOCAL AND CORPORAL MODE OF PRESENCE, AND UNION WITH THE SUBSTANTIAL ELEMENTS; but the presence itself with us we believe Holy — and indeed not imaginary, but most true, most real and most efficacious — namely that mystical Union of Christ with us which He Himself as He promises by the word and offers by the Symbols, so effects by the Spirit, and which we accept by faith and feel by Charity, according to that old saying: We feel the motion, we know not the Mode, we believe the Presence. Whence also it is plain that not virtue, efficacy, operation or benefits of Christ alone are presented and communicated to us, but first of all the VERY SUBSTANCE OF CHRIST’S BODY AND BLOOD — or that very victim given for the world’s life and slain on the cross — that through faithful Communion of this victim and Union with Christ we may consequently also be partakers of the Merits and Benefits born of His Sacrifice and as He in us so we may remain in Him. And indeed not only AS TO THE SOUL but also AS TO OUR BODY: for although as with the mouth of the body we accept the earthly thing, so with the heart’s faith as proper organ we accept the heavenly Thing — according to that old little verse: What we rub enters the belly; what we believe, the Mind — yet by that mediating faith not ONLY THE SOULS but also the BODIES THEMSELVES are brought in and united to Christ’s Body by His Spirit unto hope of resurrection and eternal life, that we may be flesh of His flesh and bone of His bones, and so one Mystical Body with Him, which the Apostle rightly says is a great Mystery.
pass_b_english: With Irenaeus: Supper = earthly + heavenly. Wittenberg Prof. VII and Torun (Marchic) n.10–13: exhibitiva signs dispense heavenly matter — not naked empty signs; Christ with all benefits offered to every eater, conferred on believers.

They deny only the LOCAL AND CORPORAL mode and substantial union with the elements — and believe the most true mystical union (motion felt, mode unknown, presence believed). What is present is the VERY SUBSTANCE of body and blood (the cross victim), uniting not soul only but our bodies too into one Mystical Body with Christ.
source_text: Quoad Præsentiam, credituri & dicturi sincerè cum Irenæo, Cœnam S. duabus rebus, scil. terrenâ & cœlesti constare. Quoad exhibitionem, vel verbis ipsius Prof. Witteberg. VII. citra omnem simulationem, pronunciaturi: Nostri (Reformati) Signa Sacramentalia Exhibitiva nominant non ratione solarum promissionum, usûs & fructûs, sed ratione materiæ, ut loqui amant, cœlestis, seu, quoniam in iis, per elementa externa & visibilia, res cœlestes ac invisibiles, non modò significantur, aut utcunque repræsentantur, sed etiam dispensantur. Quippe quod ipsum non Doctores duntaxat singuli, e. g. Trelcatius, verbis à me in Tractat. Germ. allegatis, sed & Confessiones Reform. publicæ, sigillatim Toruniensis, quæ & Marchica nostraque est, disertissimè enuntiant: Sic enim habet modò dicta Confessio de Cœnâ num. 10. ad num. 13. inclusive: Nequaquam tamen statuimus nuda, vacua, inania Signa, sed potiùs id, quod significant & obsignant, simul, vere exhibentia, tanquam certissima media & efficacia instrumenta, per quæ Corpus & Sanguis Christi, adeoque Christus ipse, cum omnibus suis beneficiis, singulis vescentibus exhibetur, seu offertur, credentibus verò confertur, donatur, & ab ipsis in cibum animæ salutarem & vivificum acceptatur. Nequaquam etiam negamus veram Corporis in Cœna præsentiam, sed tantùm LOCALEM ET CORPORALEM PRÆSENTIÆ MODUM, ET UNIONEM CUM ELEMENTIS SUBSTANTIALIBUS; Ipsam verò nobiscum præsentiam Sanctè credimus & quidem non imaginariam, sed verissimam, realissimam & efficacissimam, nempe ipsam illam Christi nobiscum Unionem mystícám, quam ipsemet ut per verbum promittit, & per Symbola offert, ita per Spiritum efficit, quamque nos per fidem acceptamus, per Charitatem sentimus, secundum vetus illud dictum: Motum sentimus, Modum nescimus, Præsentiam credimus. Unde & patet, non solam virtutem, efficaciam, operationem, aut beneficia Christi nobis præsentari, & communicari, sed imprimis IPSAM SUBSTANTIAM CORPORIS ET SANGUINIS CHRISTI, seu ipsam illam victimam, quæ pro mundi vita data est, & in cruce mactata, ut per fidelem hujus victimæ Communionem, & cum Christo Unionem, consequenter etiam Meritorum & Beneficiorum, Sacrificio ejus partorum, participes simus & sicut ipse in nobis, ita nos in ipso maneamus. Et quidem non tantùm QUOAD ANIMAM, sed etiam QUOAD CORPUS NOSTRUM: Etsi enim ut ore corporis rem terrenam, ita fide cordis, ceu organo proprio, Rem cœlestem acceptamus, secundum veterem illum versiculum: Ventrem, quod terimus, Mentem, quod credimus, intrat tamen, fide illâ mediante, non SOLUM ANIMÆ, sed & IPSA CORPORA, Christi Corpori, per ejusdem Spiritum, ad spem resurrectionis & vitæ æternæ inferuntur & uniuntur, ut simus caro de carne ejus, & os de ossibus ejus, adeóque unum cum ipso Corpus Mysticum, quod Apostolus meritò dicit Mysterium magnum esse.
